description: One phone-verification challenge sent to a GUARDIAN's number. Holds no phone number and no code in recoverable form: the number is an HMAC (key lives in site_config.json, never in the database) plus its last 4 digits for support, and the code is a pbkdf2 hash. A database dump therefore yields neither a list of guardians' numbers nor a usable code.

fields.description: HMAC-SHA256 of the E.164 number, keyed on the site encryption key. NOT the number.
fields.label: Guardian number (hashed)

fields.description: Last 4 digits only — lets a facilitator confirm "the number ending 3210?" without the app holding the number.
fields.label: Ends in

fields.description: Set for a Recovery challenge (we know whose PIN is being reset). Empty for Consent — no profile exists yet.
fields.label: Student

fields.description: pbkdf2:sha256 of the 6 digits. The code itself is never stored, logged, or recoverable.
fields.label: Code (hashed)

fields.description: Wrong guesses so far. The challenge voids at the ceiling.
fields.label: Wrong attempts

fields.description: When the right code was entered. Set once — a used challenge can never be verified again.
fields.label: Verified on

fields.description: Hash of the single-use ticket handed back after a correct code. The ticket authorises exactly ONE follow-up call (signup, or a PIN reset) for this purpose and this number.
fields.label: Ticket (hashed)

fields.description: Transport failure, for ops. Never contains the code.
fields.label: Send error

name: Hikmat OTP
